display.purpose: Kiosk status-tile numerals only; 36px, 45px at --scale 1.25. --fs-3xl (30px) is the second ten-foot step.

headline.purpose: Stat-tile numerals at the top of a detail pane.

title.purpose: Settings section h2; the metro node glyph and queue-health word read from across a room.

title-sm.purpose: The page h1 in PageHeader and a dialog title.

body.purpose: The working size: rows, controls, descriptions, buttons. Markdown prose runs at 1.6. --fs-base (16px) is the root and the pipeline charts’ floor.

label.purpose: Badges, pills, field help and errors, uppercase section headings and fieldset legends, card subtitles.

micro.purpose: Counters only: delta arrows, nav count badge, menu digit hints. Never a sentence.

mono.purpose: Inline code (0.875em on Pressed Paper), pre blocks, Kbd.

scale.purpose: Every --fs-* step is calc(rem * var(--scale)). 1 everywhere; AppShell sets 1.25 on <html> in kiosk mode. The only type-size knob.

shadows.name: floating-overlay
shadows.purpose: Dialog and Sheet panels, over a rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5) backdrop, with a 1px edge border.

shadows.name: anchored-popover
shadows.purpose: Menu, command palette, mention and export menus. No backdrop.

shadows.name: live-halo
shadows.purpose: The metro track’s active node. A status signal, not elevation; breathes to 7px/11% behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Every focus-visible ring (Tailwind ring-2 ring-accent). Buttons add a 2px canvas offset; tabs use it inset.

motion.name: transition-colors
motion.purpose: Default hover/active transition on buttons, tabs, nav items, cards, switch.

motion.name: sheet-bottom
motion.purpose: Bottom Sheet entry on a phone. motion-reduce:animate-none.

motion.name: pulse
motion.purpose: StatusPill and tier/attention dot for action-required tiers only, and the Skeleton bar. Always motion-safe:; a bare animate-pulse is a defect.

motion.name: working-shimmer
motion.purpose: The WorkingIndicator phrase while a session is mid-turn. The class is dropped under prefers-reduced-motion and the media query also neutralises it.

motion.name: metro-pulse
motion.purpose: Only a live track’s active node; legend swatches never pulse. Gated on prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: reduced-motion-gate
motion.purpose: One JS subscriber (useViewport().reducedMotion) plus motion-safe:/motion-reduce: utilities. Nothing animates when the viewer asks it not to.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.note: Custom variant: a phone in portrait; sheds secondary chrome (pill labels, header controls).

breakpoints.name: short
breakpoints.note: Custom variant: keyboard-up or landscape phone; sheds optional chrome.

breakpoints.name: charts
breakpoints.note: Pipeline charts reflow (nodes flex, Gantt name takes its own line). Also a desktop at 200% zoom.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.note: The desktop breakpoint; CardFrame and the shell branch on it.

breakpoints.name: kiosk
breakpoints.note: ?kiosk=1: read-only, --scale 1.25, no dialogs or page actions, idle cursor hidden, queue train wraps in portrait.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one primary action on a surface: Save, Confirm, New. Signal Blue fill, Ink-on-Blue text, 40px (md); use the 44px lg size for a dialog confirm.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The default button for anything that is not the primary action. Sheet White, hairline border, Slate Ink; hover fills with Pressed Paper.

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Destructive confirm (Delete, Discard and leave). Stop Red theme-invariant -strong fill with Fill Ink so it reads the same in both themes; always 44px tall in a dialog footer.

components.name: Text Input (Field)
components.description: A labelled control: 14px/500 label, 40px (min 44px) Sheet White input with hairline border, Graphite placeholder, accent border + 2px ring on focus, 12px Graphite help. Error turns border and ring Stop Red.
components.html: Shown in the list and the browser tab.

components.name: Status Pill
components.description: Tone text on tone wash, 12px/500, full pill, with a 12px glyph so the state is never colour alone. Count badges are the same pill without the icon, in neutral.
components.html: Ready Needs you 12

components.name: Tabs
components.description: The page tab strip: hairline baseline, 44px tabs at 14px/500, Graphite at rest with a transparent 2px underline, Signal Blue text and underline when selected; count badges and the amber attention dot ride inside the tab.

components.name: Status Tile Strip
components.description: The pipeline number band: wash-on-hairline tiles, 6px corners, toned 20px/600 numeral over an uppercase Graphite label; empty tiles dim to 50%, the active filter takes the accent ring. On the kiosk the numeral grows to the 36px display step.

components.name: List Card with Tone Rail
components.description: The CardFrame every sessions and roadmap row shares: Sheet White, hairline, 10px corners, a 3px tone rail set into the left edge, 14px/500 title with a tier dot, 12px Graphite subtitle naming the tier, a trailing pill. Hover strengthens the border; selection is an accent ring on Blue Tint.

components.css: .ds-track{display:flex;align-items:flex-start;max-width:440px;font-family:system-ui,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif;}.ds-node{display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;flex-shrink:0;width:84px}.ds-node-c{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;width:32px;height:32px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--t-edge,#d9dde3);color:var(--t-ink-muted,#646a77);font-size:20px}.ds-node-done .ds-node-c{background:var(--t-success-strong,#15803d);color:var(--t-on-strong,#fff)}.ds-node-active .ds-node-c{background:var(--t-accent,#2461e7);color:var(--t-canvas,#f6f7f9);box-shadow:0 0 0 4px color-mix(in srgb,var(--t-accent,#2461e7) 22%,transparent)}.ds-node-fail .ds-node-c{background:var(--t-danger,#c23636);color:var(--t-canvas,#f6f7f9)}.ds-node-parked .ds-node-c{background:var(--t-warning-strong,#9a5d00);color:var(--t-on-strong,#fff);font-weight:700}.ds-node-label{margin-top:3px;font-size:16px;color:var(--t-ink-muted,#646a77)}.ds-node-active .ds-node-label{color:var(--t-accent,#2461e7);font-weight:700}.ds-node-parked .ds-node-label{color:var(--t-warning,#9a5d00);font-weight:700}.ds-node-eta{font-size:16px;color:var(--t-accent,#2461e7);font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}.ds-seg{flex:1;min-width:24px;height:4px;margin-top:14px;border-radius:2px;background:var(--t-edge,#d9dde3)}.ds-seg-done{background:var(--t-success,#147c3b)}@media (prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference){.ds-node-active .ds-node-c{animation:ds-metro-pulse 1.5s infinite}}@keyframes ds-metro-pulse{0%,100%{box-shadow:0 0 0 4px color-mix(in srgb,var(--t-accent,#2461e7) 22%,transparent)}50%{box-shadow:0 0 0 7px color-mix(in srgb,var(--t-accent,#2461e7) 11%,transparent)}}

narrative.overview:
A race team's pit wall is a bank of quiet screens read at a glance by one person who is responsible for everything on them. Nothing on the wall is decorative; the only colour is status, the controls are few and deliberate, and the same screens are read from a stool and from across the garage. ViberPit's interface is built the same way. It is a console for one operator who is interrupt-driven: the queue of things that need a human is the product, and everything else is calm, dense context around it. (Alternates, if the owner prefers: **"The Instrument Panel"** or **"The Dispatch Desk"**. Swap the name; the rules below do not change.)

The material is near-neutral paper and ink. Surfaces are flat white or cool grey, separated by hairlines rather than shadows; depth is a one-step tonal lift (`surface` → `surface-raised`) and a border, and a drop shadow appears only under the three things that actually float (dialog, sheet, menu). There is exactly one interactive accent, a signal blue used for focus rings, the selected tab, the active nav item and the primary button, and four status tones (success, warning, danger, info) plus a neutral, each with a text value, a tint and a theme-invariant fill. Status is always a tone *and* a word or glyph, never a colour alone. Type is the system face at a small working size, 14px body on a 4px grid, with weight (500/600/700) doing the hierarchical work rather than size. The kiosk reads the same screens at ten feet by multiplying one variable, not by a second design.

The voice is serious about the work, not about itself. Density, speed and glanceability beat explanation. Confirmed rejections, all enforced in code: no brand colour in the UI (the Viper Green logotype is the one exception and is text-exempt), no webfonts, no hard-coded colour outside `index.css` (an ESLint rule and a contrast test fail the build), no dark-mode class variants (the tokens flip at `:root`), and no motion that is not a live signal.
keyCharacteristics: Near-neutral ink/edge/surface palette with one accent and four status tones; every pair held at ≥ 4.5:1 in light and dark by a test.
Flat surfaces, 1px hairline borders, one tonal step for raised chrome; shadows only on floating overlays.
System type (`system-ui`) on a 4px rhythm; 14px body, 12px labels, weight carries hierarchy.
One type scale: the kiosk sets `--scale: 1.25` and every size follows.
44px minimum target on every control a finger can reach; `focus-visible` ring in the accent everywhere.
Status rails, dots and pills carry tone; the word or glyph beside them carries the meaning.
Motion is rare, short (150–200ms) and always behind `motion-safe` / `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Four layout modes (phone, tablet, desktop, kiosk) from one shell; chrome is shed, never shrunk, when the viewport is short or narrow.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue is the only interactive colour. If something is blue it is focusable, selected, active or live; nothing is blue for emphasis.

rules.name: The Logotype-Only Rule
rules.body: Brand colours are never UI tokens. Viper Green appears in the wordmark and nowhere a person reads, points or taps; Vibe Purple does not appear at all.

rules.name: The Tone-Plus-Word Rule
rules.body: A status is a tone and a word or glyph together (pill: icon + label; tier: rail/dot + the tier named in the subtitle; failed bars: colour + hatch texture). Colour alone never carries a state.

rules.name: The Invariant Fill Rule
rules.body: `-strong` fills and `on-strong` ink are declared once and never flip with the theme, so white-on-fill stays AA in both. Ink on a plain `accent` fill is `accent-ink`, never white.

rules.name: The One Scale Rule
rules.body: There is one type scale. The kiosk enlarges it by setting `--scale: 1.25` on `<html>` and nothing else; a second kiosk-only size rule anywhere is a defect.

rules.name: The Read Ink Rule
rules.body: Text a person reads is Slate Ink or Graphite (both ≥ 4.5:1). Pencil Grey (`ink-faint`) is for icons and decoration only. Placeholders are read, so they are Graphite at full opacity, set once in `@layer base`.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: Within a row or card, hierarchy is weight and ink, not size: title 14px/500 Slate, subtitle 12px Graphite. Size steps are reserved for page, section and numeral levels.

rules.name: The 44px Rule
rules.body: Every control a finger can reach is at least 44px tall (`min-h-target`): tabs, nav items, icon buttons, inputs at `md`, menu items, list cards, the `lg` button that every destructive or primary confirm action in a dialog footer must use. Dense desktop controls lift the floor only behind `@media (hover: hover)`.

rules.name: The Shed-Not-Shrink Rule
rules.body: When a viewport is short or narrow, optional chrome is hidden with the `short:` / `narrow:` variants; the title is never squeezed to make room.

rules.name: The Panes-Scroll Rule
rules.body: The document never scrolls. A page that can scroll past the viewport is a bug, not a layout.

rules.name: The Hairline-First Rule
rules.body: A boundary is a 1px `edge` border before it is anything else. Reach for a tonal step second, and for a shadow only when the element portals out of the page flow.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Nothing is lifted at rest. Hover is a fill change (to Pressed Paper) or a border change (to Rule Grey); selection is a 2px accent ring plus Blue Tint; focus is the same 2px accent ring.

dos: **Do** take every colour from a `--t-*` token through its Tailwind namespace (`bg-surface`, `text-ink-muted`, `border-edge`); the ESLint `no-raw-palette` rule and `contrast.test.ts` are the gate.
**Do** keep status as tone plus word or glyph: a `StatusPill` with its icon, a tier rail with the tier named in the subtitle, a failed bar with its hatch.
**Do** put `text-on-strong` on any `-strong` fill and `text-accent-ink` on a plain `accent` fill; never `text-white`.
**Do** give every reachable control a 44px minimum (`min-h-target`) and the 2px Signal Blue `focus-visible` ring; use the `lg` button for a dialog's confirm or destructive action.
**Do** gate every animation behind `motion-safe:` (or `motion-reduce:animate-none`) and animate only a live signal: one needs-you dot, one active node, one working shimmer.
**Do** separate with a 1px Hairline Grey border or a step to Pressed Paper before reaching for anything else; reserve shadows for dialog, sheet and menu.
**Do** write Graphite for secondary text and placeholders (5.4:1), and reserve Pencil Grey for icons and decoration.
**Do** make headings carry hierarchy by weight (600) and level, not by size jumps; keep the page `h1` in `PageHeader` and section headings as 12px uppercase Graphite.
**Do** shed optional chrome with `short:` and `narrow:` when a phone runs out of room, and keep the title.
donts: **Don't** use Viper Green or Vibe Purple anywhere a person reads, points or taps; the wordmark is the only home for `brand`.
**Don't** add a webfont, a `dark:` variant, a literal hex outside `index.css`, or a second `--on-wash`-style token family.
**Don't** add a kiosk-only size, a second `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)` subscriber in JS, or a second scale: `--scale` is the one knob.
**Don't** convey a state by colour alone, or hide a setting's description behind a tooltip.
**Don't** let a tree of dots or a legend swatch pulse; motion belongs to the one live element on screen.
**Don't** lift a card at rest, add a shadow to a header, tile or input, or signal hover by elevation; hover is a fill or border change.
**Don't** let the document scroll, render a dialog on the kiosk, or render disabled page actions on it; the wall shows the title and the numbers.
**Don't** use a sentence at the 11px Micro step; it is for counters.
